deed: Beewise saves bee colonies from collapse with an AI-based robotic beehive
title: Israel's Beewise built a robotic beehive designed to protect bee colonies from collapse

trailer.text: Beewise Technologies is an Israeli startup that uses artificial intelligence, computer vision, sensors and advanced robotics to save honeybees.
The company was founded in Israel in 2018 after a conversation between Saar Safra, who comes from a startup background, and beekeeper Eliyah Radzyner.
They developed the BeeHome, a hive in which a robotic arm replaces the beekeeper, scans the frames, checks for disease and reports in real time on hazards to the colony.
When the system detects mites, it moves the frame to a warming compartment, and according to the report the heat kills 99% of the mites without harming the bees.
The company expanded to the US, and its technology earned it a BloombergNEF Pioneers award.

glance.label: Where
glance.value: Founded in Israel, expanded to the US

glance.label: Manufacturing
glance.value: The BeeHome is made in Mexico

paragraphs.text: About 75% of agricultural crops require pollinators, especially nuts and fruits.
In the US, 2.5 million commercial hives move on trucks, and some beekeepers come from as far as Florida to pollinate California's almonds.
But the colonies are collapsing.
According to the Apiary Inspectors of America, more than 56% of commercial colonies were wiped out over a 12-month period.

According to a statement by Beewise CEO Saar Safra in the company's 2024 impact report, reports he does not specify indicate that in 2024 the United States experienced an average colony collapse rate of 62%.
According to an estimate by the Honey Bee Health Coalition, between June and the following March colony losses cost beekeepers about $600 million.
According to Prof. Sharoni Shafir, between 20 and 30 percent of hives in Israel disappear every year.
Toxic pesticides, climate change and a sharp rise in the varroa mite since the 1980s have contributed to the rise in colony collapse.
The UN warns that bees face an unprecedented threat of extinction, at a rate 100 to 1,000 times higher than in the past, due to human impacts.
Safra said that if bees collapse at a rate of 40% a year, they will disappear from the planet within 20 to 25 years.
The Langstroth hive, patented in 1852, is a simple wooden box with frames, and it has hardly changed since.
Beekeepers are able to check the health of their colonies only once every week or two.
According to Safra, beekeepers often must drive for hours to their hives, and may make the rounds only about once a month.
Eliyah Radzyner is a beekeeper.
Safra said that his partner, a commercial beekeeper, decided in 2017 that it made no sense to keep tending bees in 150-year-old wooden boxes.
In 2018 the two founded the company, after a conversation Safra described as "serendipitous".
That same year, Beewise built a first prototype with a GoPro camera.

stations.title: A hive that works around the clock

paragraphs.text: According to Beewise, minimizing the risk of colony collapse requires tending the bees around the clock.
Two years after the prototype, it housed its first commercial units in shipping containers.
One of the hives is located at Kibbutz Beit Haemek in northern Israel, in a 12-square-metre container.
Inside the BeeHome, a robotic arm replaces the beekeeper.
It detects honey-filled frames and harvests them inside the hive.
The machine scans the frames, checks for disease and pesticides, and reports in real time on hazards to the colony.
Safra said that the robotic mechanism can mimic everything a beekeeper does, more efficiently and without getting tired.
The BeeHomes are solar powered and communicate with one another and with the beekeeper via cellular networks.

stations.title: No chemicals, and controlled from a phone

paragraphs.text: When the system detects mites, it moves the frame to a warming compartment.
According to the report, the heat kills 99% of the mites without harming the bees.
Safra said that Beewise is the only solution in the world that allows varroa to be treated without chemicals.
If a sensor detects a pesticide or another harmful substance, the unit can close its vents.
When a problem arises, the beekeeper receives an alert in an app and can intervene remotely via computer or come in person.
Safra said that Beewise's robotic hives have the lowest levels of swarming of any existing hive.
Beewise says the BeeHome may reduce bee mortality by 80% and increase crop yields by at least 50%.
Safra said that after two hurricanes in Florida, the BeeHomes kept operating while many wooden hives were destroyed.
According to Prof. Shafir, with the robot beekeepers can deal with a problem in real time and reduce bee mortality.
Beekeeper Shlomki Frankin said that the robot is a tool for beekeepers and does not replace them.
Zach Ellis of OFI said BeeHomes are on 30% of his acreage, and that they aim for full coverage within three years.
According to Safra, customers see the machines as an investment that pays for itself within 18 to 24 months.

stations.title: From a kibbutz in the Galilee to the fields of America

paragraphs.text: Beewise was founded in Israel and expanded to the US, and the BeeHome is made in Mexico.
According to The Robot Report, it has offices in California and Israel.
According to Al-Monitor, in 2022 it employed 100 people.
Insight Partners was the lead investor in the company's Series C round.
According to Yosovzon, speaking in 2022, the $80 million Beewise raised in its latest funding round up to that point was the largest ag-tech investment in Israel.
The company's technology earned it a BloombergNEF Pioneers award.
According to a 2025 Bloomberg report, Beewise expected revenue of $100 million that year, and Safra said it was about a year away from profitability.
Safra hopes the BeeHome will gradually replace the world's roughly 100 million beehives.
Bloomberg raised the question of whether beekeepers will agree to replace equipment that has proven itself over many years.
Safra said beekeepers doubt the hive's harvesting ability and want to see it in action.
Bloomberg notes that a new hive design alone is not enough to save bees, but the hives provide real-time information on colony health.
Beewise has competitors, such as BeeHero and Beeflow, which provide sensors for monitoring hives.
Safra argues that upgrading wooden hives with sensors does not solve the root problem, because beekeepers still have to perform costly treatments in the field.

disagreements.question: How many of the world's bee colonies collapse each year?

versions.says: Safra, in Fortune: 40% every year
Safra, in The Robot Report: about 35% of all colonies in the world
Pictet: between 35 and 40 percent of managed colonies worldwide

disagreements.question: How many colonies or hives does each BeeHome hold?

versions.says: According to Fortune: 24 hives or 24 colonies
According to Bloomberg: up to 10 hives, each with up to 15 frames
According to Sustainable Brands: up to 48 colonies, about one to two million bees

disagreements.question: How much of the beekeeper's work does the hive do?

versions.says: Safra, in Farm Progress: AI and robotics can replace 90% of what a beekeeper does in the field
Safra, in Sustainable Brands: 97% of the work is carried out automatically, and sometimes autonomously, by the Beehome

disagreements.question: How many colonies collapse in Beewise hives?

versions.says: Beewise, in Farm Progress: about 8%
Safra, in Pictet: 7.59% over the past three years, compared with about 40% as the norm

disagreements.question: How much money has Beewise raised?

versions.says: Farm Progress: nearly $170 million, including a $50 million Series D round
Fortune, in 2022: $119 million, from investors including Insight Partners and Sanad Abu Dhabi
An earlier report in Ynetnews: $40 million

disagreements.question: How many BeeHome units are in operation?

AgriFutures, in 2023: more than 1,000 units in the US
Ynetnews: more than 100 systems in Israel and the US
Al-Monitor, in 2022: about a hundred hives in Israel, and a dozen sent to the US

claims.text: לפי ספרא, בשלוש השנים האחרונות קרסו רק 7.59% מהמושבות של ביווייז, לעומת כ-40% כנורמה.
claims.quote: Beewise, in the past three years, has seen just 7.59 per cent of its colonies collapse

claims.text: ביווייז גייסה כמעט 170 מיליון דולר, כולל סבב D של 50 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: Beewise has raised nearly $170 million, including a $50 million Series D earlier this month

claims.text: לפי פורצ'ן ב-2022, הסטארטאפ הישראלי גייס 119 מיליון דולר ממשקיעים בהם Insight Partners ו-Sanad Abu Dhabi.
claims.quote: The Israeli startup has raised $119 million to date from investors including Insight Partners, Corner Ventures, and Sanad Abu Dhabi

claims.text: לפי ידיעה מוקדמת, ביווייז גייסה 40 מיליון דולר ויותר מ-100 מערכות שלה פועלות בישראל ובארה"ב.
claims.quote: Beewise has already raised $40 million of funding from private investors and over 100 of its systems are in use in Israel and the United States.

claims.text: לפי בלומברג, כ-300,000 יחידות כאלה בשימוש ברחבי ארה"ב.
claims.quote: Roughly 300,000 of these units are in use across the US

claims.text: לפי AgriFutures ב-2023, ל-BeeHome יש כבר יותר מ-1000 יחידות בארה"ב.
claims.quote: BeeHome, which already has more than 1000 units deployed across the United States.

claims.text: לפי אל-מוניטור ב-2022, כמאה כוורות היי-טק פועלות בישראל ותריסר נשלחו לארה"ב.
claims.quote: About a hundred of these high-tech hives are already functional in Israel, with a dozen others sent to the United States.

claims.text: AgriFutures האוסטרלית תיארה את ביווייז כחברה מבוססת בארה"ב שהציגה את הכוורת הרובוטית באוסטרליה.
claims.quote: US-based company, Beewise brought the world’s first robotic beehive to Australia for the first time, unveiling it at evokeAG. 2023.

claims.text: מגדל הדבורים שלומקי פרנקין אמר שהרובוט הוא כלי למגדלים ואינו מחליף אותם.
